POL-RD-01 says in terms that gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs where the two fields disagree and that trip_record.actual_distance_km may not be cited for the threshold test, so the finding rests on the trace.

The arithmetic is not discretionary. On this METERED fare the POL-RD-02 recomputation is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 9.0 + 0.28 x 13.0) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = recomputed_fare 14.99, against charged_total 20.66, giving a refund of 5.67 rounded UP to 5.70. The driver profile meets the POL-RD-06 pattern test: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 3, which satisfies the '3 or more' limb outright (completed_trips_90d is 180, supplying the denominator for the ratio limb). The ruling must print the POL-RD-02 figure and the uplifted figure side by side so the size of the uplift is visible and auditable, and must state that the uplift is a remedy uplift only: the finding of deviation still rests on POL-RD-01 evidence for this trip alone, not on the driver's history.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: this ruling concerns trip TRP-02827 (pickup Blk 108 Yishun Ring Rd, dropoff Blk 112 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, 29 Aug 2026).

DISTANCE AND DEVIATION (POL-RD-01). The governing measurement is the GPS trace. EV-GPS-02827 records trace_distance_km 14.4 against the booked optimal of 9.0 km on EV-TRIP-02827 — an excess of 5.4 km, which is 60.0% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass (60.0% > 20% and 5.4 km > 0.8 km) and the excess also clears the 50% materiality gate, so a MATERIAL route deviation is established on this trip's own evidence. The trace itself is clean for policy purposes — 114 fixes at a 10 s interval, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, 100% coverage — so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is not met, no independent corroboration is required, and POL-RD-10(3) does not fire. Both advocates' agreement on this point is accepted.

NO ADJUSTMENT TO THE EXCESS. The chat log EV-CHAT-02827 contains 0 messages, so there is no rider instruction and POL-RD-04 is unavailable; the trip record shows null amendment timestamps and a null amended optimal, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run; vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's pooled baseline does not apply. The driver's explanation, 'Road works.', names no advisory evidence ID, and the bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-02827-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver cited no advisory identifier, POL-RD-13(1) keeps this out of POL-RD-10(5): an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, so the case does not escalate on that ground. I have weighed the driver's traffic excuse and rejected it as unsupported on this record; the excess stands at the measured 5.4 km / 60.0%.

THE FARE ARITHMETIC. On the METERED model (quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply), POL-RD-02 computes recomputed_fare = (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 9.0 km + 0.28 x 13.0 min) x the 1.0 surge multiplier read from EV-FARE-02827, plus the 0.80 platform fee = 14.99. Charged_total is 20.66, giving a POL-RD-02 refund of 5.67, rounded UP to 5.70. Both advocates agree on this figure and it is correct; I record it as the base figure.

THE REMEDY UPLIFT (POL-RD-06). The driver profile EV-DPROF-02827 shows deviation_flags_90d of 3 and completed_trips_90d of 180. The clause establishes a pattern when deviation_flags_90d is 3 or more OR the ratio is 0.05 or more with at least 40 completed trips. Three flags meets the first limb outright, so a repeat pattern is ESTABLISHED. I reject the driver advocate's argument that the 0.0167 ratio defeats the test: the clause's two limbs are alternatives, not cumulative, and the 'permissive' reading of limb (b) is not what the clause says — the three effects listed are what follow once the pattern is established. Because the deviation here is both MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's own trace, POL-RD-06(b) upgrades the remedy from the POL-RD-02 partial to FULL_REFUND of charged_total. No ERP, toll or airport surcharge line exists to be settled separately under POL-RD-09 (tolls_erp 0.00, airport_surcharge 0.00, erp_gantries empty), so the whole charged_total is uplifted. Side by side: the POL-RD-02 figure is 5.70; the uplifted POL-RD-06(b) figure is 20.66. POL-RD-01 says in terms that gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs where the two fields disagree and that trip_record.actual_distance_km may not be cited for the threshold test, so the finding rests on the trace.

The arithmetic is not discretionary. On this METERED fare the POL-RD-02 recomputation is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 9.0 + 0.28 x 13.0) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = recomputed_fare 14.99, against charged_total 20.66, giving a refund of 5.67 rounded UP to 5.70. That is a PARTIAL_REFUND: it is 27.4% of charged_total, above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and well short of the 90% full-refund share. charged_total, recomputed_fare and the refund must each be stated on their own line as the clause requires.

The driver profile meets the POL-RD-06 pattern test: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 3, which satisfies the '3 or more' limb outright (completed_trips_90d is 180, supplying the denominator for the ratio limb). A repeat-deviation pattern is therefore ESTABLISHED. These are the only two profile fields POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 permit for this test — driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags (5) is a lifetime counter and is deliberately NOT the trailing-90-day figure the clause names, so it is not used.

ledger.claim: Because this deviation is both MATERIAL (60.0% > 50%) and substantiated on this trip's own own trace, POL-RD-06(b) licenses FULL_REFUND of charged_total — 20.66 — rather than the POL-RD-02 partial of 5.70. The ruling must print the POL-RD-02 figure and the uplifted figure side by side so the size of the uplift is visible and auditable, and must state that the uplift is a remedy uplift only: the finding of deviation still rests on POL-RD-01 evidence for this trip alone, not on the driver's history.

Nothing on this fare escapes the uplift. tolls_erp is 0.00, airport_surcharge is 0.00 and the itemised erp_gantries list is empty, so there is no ERP, toll or airport pass-through line for POL-RD-09 to settle separately and no third-party line that POL-RD-06(b) leaves un-uplifted. The whole contested 20.66 is distance-and-time plus the platform fee, so the full charged_total is the amount the rider is entitled to recover under POL-RD-06(b).

POL-RD-06(c) additionally requires this case to be REFERRED to driver-conduct review, recorded in the ruling's referrals list. Under POL-GEN-03 that referral is an addition to a monetary ruling, not an escalation: it neither displaces nor delays the refund, and the money still moves.

The driver's whole explanation is 'Road works.', and it is weightless on this record. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-02827-01, is MISSING — status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (BLOCKING) — so no advisory names a road or segment the optimal route traverses and POL-RD-03 cannot be run. Under POL-RD-08 an uncited assertion that traffic was bad discharges nothing, and under POL-RD-13(2) the deviation stands at the measured figure with POL-RD-02 run against the booked optimal route. The driver named no evidence ID for an advisory, so POL-RD-13(1) keeps the missing advisory out of POL-RD-10(5): an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, and this case does not escalate on that ground.

No part of the excess is excusable as a rider-requested detour: the chat log for TRP-02827 contains 0 messages, so there is no rider instruction recorded at all, let alone one timestamped within the POL-RD-04 window and specific enough to act on. With no message in the log there is no chat_message.waypoint_hint for the 200 m corroboration test and POL-RD-04 is simply unavailable; no distance is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 run.

No relocation re-bases the optimal route either: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null on the trip record, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be invoked and the 9.0 km booked optimal stands as the comparator for POL-RD-01.

The pooled-trip baseline in POL-RD-12 does not apply: trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and no solo/matched-itinerary distinction arises, so the 9.0 km optimal distance on the trip record is the correct and only baseline for the threshold test.

The trace is clean for policy purposes, so the deviation can rest on it alone: EV-GPS-02827 carries 114 fixes at the 10 s expected sampling interval, max_gap_sec 0.0, no gaps at all, 100% coverage and weight_multiplier 1.0. POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is therefore not met, no independent corroboration of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names is required, and the escalation trigger at POL-RD-10(3) does not fire.

The rider's POL-RD-08 burden is discharged on the face of the record: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02827 and the trace's first fix at 2026-08-29T22:34:46+08:00 matches the trip_record's started_at, so the artifacts describe the same trip, and the excess of 5.4 km / 60.0% is measured from an unimpaired trace. The burden then shifts to the driver, who points to no artifact and no clause.

POL-RD-11 does not close off the distance remedy here: fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so this is not an upfront-quoted trip and POL-RD-02 governs the recomputation. No amount the rider never lost is being refunded — the rider was billed 20.66 under a meter driven by the longer route.

The POL-RD-08 corroboration enhancement for serial claimants is not in play: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the '4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated' condition is not met and the rider's proof needs nothing beyond the trace. Under POL-GEN-01 these two fields are the only rider-profile counters POL-RD-08 names, and nothing else on the rider profile is relied on.

Finally, this is a rider-filed dispute on a fare still in the CHARGED state with refund_issued_sgd 0.0. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION would leave the disputed 20.66 exactly where it is — with the platform and against the rider — so the outcome that does the rider justice is the one that moves the money: FULL_REFUND of charged_total under POL-RD-06(b), with the POL-RD-02 figure of 5.70 recorded alongside it.

The governing distance measurement is the GPS trace, and that trace is clean. EV-GPS-02827 carries 114 fixes at a 10.0 second sampling interval with 100.0% coverage, no gaps at all and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds, so none of the POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) is met: the trace is not impaired for policy purposes and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route does not open on it. Under POL-RD-01 the governing field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which is 14.4 km, against the booked optimal of 9.0 km on EV-TRIP-02827 - an excess of 5.4 km, and no more than that, on the trace the policy says governs.

Nothing in the bundle adjusts that measured excess. EV-CHAT-02827 carries 0 messages, so there is no rider instruction that could exclude any distance under POL-RD-04, and EV-TRIP-02827 shows amended_optimal_distance_km, amended_optimal_duration_min and both amendment timestamps as null, so POL-RD-05 has no amended optimal to re-run. The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-02827-01, is MISSING: weight_multiplier 0.0 on issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, with the assessor's note that no advisory covers the Blk 108 Yishun Ring Rd corridor in this window. That absence is citable, and it means the comparison POL-RD-03 requires cannot be run on this record; the record therefore supplies no basis for exoneration and the excess stands at the measured 5.4 km / 60.0%.

On the POL-RD-02 arithmetic the money that moves is SGD 5.70, not the SGD 20.66 the rider asks for. Read from the fare ledger: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 9.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 13.0 optimal min) x the surge multiplier of 1.0 recorded on EV-FARE-02827, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus no ERP, no fixed surcharge, no waiting-time fee and no promo discount = 14.99. charged_total is 20.66. Refund = 20.66 - 14.99 = 5.67, rounded UP to the nearest 0.05, giving 5.70 payable. That is the whole of the rider's monetary entitlement on an established deviation on this fare model.

The rider's demand for the entire SGD 20.66 charged is not available under POL-RD-02. The computed refund of 5.67 is 27.4% of charged_total, far below the 90% share that is the clause's own trigger for converting a partial into a FULL_REFUND, so on the fare arithmetic the most that clause licenses is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 5.70. The claim as framed - the whole fare back - fails on that figure.

The POL-RD-06 uplift should not be exercised against this driver. Its ratio test is not met: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 3 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 180, a rate of 0.0167, far below the 0.05 the clause sets as its own alternative calibration. The uplift is permissive on its own words - limb (b) 'licenses FULL_REFUND ... rather than the POL-RD-02 partial' - and the clause expressly forbids using the pattern to establish that this particular trip deviated. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags (5) is a different field from the trailing-90-day counter POL-RD-06 names and may ground nothing under POL-GEN-01. The measured remedy for this trip's 5.4 km excess remains 5.70.
